title: Student Gradebook
story: A teacher with 30 students, 5 subjects each, assignments, weighted averages, letter grades, and report cards. Managing this on paper is a nightmare. Build the gradebook — track students, subjects, grades, calculate averages, identify top performers, and print report cards. Using contracts to guarantee grade validity.
why: The gradebook combines structs, Vec, Map for subject grades, weighted averages, grade scale mapping, sorting for rankings, and contracts — a complete educational data system.
analogy: A teacher's gradebook spreadsheet with rows of students and columns of assignments. The final column uses a formula to calculate the weighted average, then maps it to A/B/C/D/F. Your gradebook IS that spreadsheet, with contracts ensuring no grade slips outside the valid range.
try_it: Add weighted grades: tests=50%, homework=30%, participation=20%. Add grade distribution histogram. Identify students at risk (average below 60%). Add extra credit that can boost scores up to 105%. Implement ranking: 1st, 2nd, 3rd place.
tips: Contracts on add_grade guarantee values stay in valid range (0-100)
Calculate weighted average: sum(score × weight) / sum(weights)
Rank by sorting students by average descending — index 0 = top performer
common_mistakes: Adding grades with score > max_score — contract should reject these
Averaging unweighted when subjects have different credit hours
Printing report cards for students with no grades — handle empty gracefully
